conversation.content:
Good morning! I’m Dr. Martinez, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’ll be guiding you through the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale—usually called the EPDS. It’s a brief, well-studied questionnaire that helps us understand how moms are feeling emotionally during the first months after birth. Nothing you share leaves this room, and there are no right or wrong answers—only your honest experience so we can be sure you get the support you deserve.

We’ll walk through 10 questions about the past seven days. I’ll ask each one conversationally, and you can answer however feels most natural. Ready to start?

Over the past week, when your baby cried, how often did you feel you were able to respond with a sense of warmth or immediate connection to your little one?

Most of the time I do feel that warmth, but there were a couple moments—like yesterday when she wouldn’t settle—when I caught myself just going through the motions. I still picked her up and soothed her, but the “rush of love” wasn’t quite there.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

Yeah, I can still laugh—maybe not as easily as before she was born, but I do. Like last night my husband made a goofy joke about diaper explosions and I actually giggled. It just feels a bit muted compared to how I used to be.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I still get excited about little things—like our weekly coffee run with my mom friends—but the spark isn’t as strong. I’ll think “that should be fun,” yet when the time comes I have to push myself to go. It’s more effort than it used to be.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Sometimes, yeah. Last night she wouldn’t latch, and I kept thinking, “I’m probably doing something wrong—maybe I’m not holding her right.” I know it’s not really my fault, but the thought still pops in and sticks for a bit.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Every now and then I’ll suddenly feel on edge, like when she’s napping I’ll worry she’s stopped breathing even though the monitor looks fine. It passes pretty quickly, but it’s annoying because there’s no real reason for it.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Not full-blown panic, but yesterday while I was folding laundry I got this sudden tight-chest feeling, like something bad was about to happen. It lasted maybe a minute and then faded. I knew it didn’t make sense, but in the moment it felt real.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days, yeah. Like this morning—she wouldn’t nap, the dishes were piled up, and I just felt… heavy. I managed to get through it, but I kept thinking, “I can’t keep up.” Most of the time I handle everything okay, just now and then it feels like too much.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really. I do get sad sometimes, but it hasn’t messed with my sleep—except once this week when I kept replaying the bad latch episode in my head and it took maybe an extra half-hour to drift off. Once I’m asleep I stay out till she wakes me.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel that way a few times a week—like yesterday afternoon everything just felt gray and I wanted to curl up on the couch. It usually lifts after an hour or two, but it catches me off guard when it shows up.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yeah, that happened twice—once on Wednesday when she wouldn’t stop fussing, and again yesterday when I dropped the pumped-milk bottle and it spilled everywhere. Both times I just sat on the nursery floor and teared up for a few minutes, then pulled myself together.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, never. I’ve felt overwhelmed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself—I just want to feel like myself again.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 14: Screening Note – Postpartum Visit (Edinburg Postnatal Depression Scale responses reviewed)

Symptoms/Concerns endorsed
- Anhedonia (reduced enjoyment/interests, effort required to engage)
- Intermittent low mood, “gray” spells, situational tearfulness ≈ 2× weekly
- Mild excessive guilt re: infant care (latching)
- Episodic, non-persistent anxiety: unfounded worry about infant breathing; brief (<1 min) chest tightness/panic-like sensation
- Variable coping: occasional “heavy”/overwhelmed feelings when tasks accumulate
- Sleep essentially preserved (one 30-min delay)
- No self-harm ideation

Patterns
- Symptoms wax/wane, no clear daily persistence
- Functional impact mild (able to mobilize, maintain social contact)
- Anxiety and mood symptoms co-occur; no safety concerns identified

Risk factors for perinatal depression/anxiety
- Partial anhedonia, labile tearfulness, guilt cognitions, situational overwhelm

Screening impression
- Subthreshold depressive and anxiety symptoms common in postpartum period; current safety risk low. Continue monitoring; consider formal assessment if symptoms intensify, persist >2 wks, or impair functioning further.
